papers_read.title_as_printed: Differential Role for Hippocampal Subfields in Alzheimer's Disease Progression Revealed with Deep Learning (Kwak et al., Cerebral Cortex 2022)
Predicting the progression of mild cognitive impairment based on fine-grained and spatiotemporal features of MRI (Hu et al., Biomed. Signal Process. Control 2025)

what_each_reports.P-182: Hippocampal-box DenseNet trained on AD vs CN, applied to baseline sMRI of 381 ADNI-2/GO MCI subjects (follow-up at least 18 months); Acc 75.85%, AUC 0.777.
what_each_reports.P-122: MMS-TransENet (CNN-Transformer) on pairs of longitudinal whole-brain 2D axial slice stacks (two time points); pMCI = progression within 3 years (DSM-5), ADNI 1/GO/2/3; 823 longitudinal samples from 275 subjects; held-out test of 124 samples Acc 84.74%, AUC 0.8587; six-fold CV 84.28% +/- 1.65. Own ablations without the multi-scale modules: 71.6% and 76.5%.

quantity_a: Subject-level accuracy from a single baseline T1 hippocampal region, AD/CN-transfer model, 381 MCI, follow-up of at least 18 months.
quantity_b: Sample-level accuracy from paired two-time-point whole-brain axial slices, model trained on MCI labels, 3-year progression criterion, test of 124 longitudinal samples.
incompatible_if_same: Unclear, and moot: the unit of analysis differs (subjects vs longitudinal samples drawn several per subject), and P-122's architecture ablations without its longitudinal multi-scale modules (71.6-76.5%) bracket P-182's 75.85%, so neither study refutes an ordering the other claims.

gates.task: match nominally (T2), but the horizons differ (3 years vs at least 18 months).
gates.dataset_family: match: ADNI in both; overlap possible.
gates.validation_tier: match: both internal ADNI held-out testing.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: same metric name (accuracy) but different unit of analysis (subjects vs longitudinal samples), different input representation (one baseline scan vs two time points), different training target (AD/CN transfer vs direct pMCI/sMCI) and different horizon.
performance_validity: flag does not apply: 0.8474 and 0.7585 are below 0.97; both flags false.
independence: Distinct author groups; both ADNI (ADNI-2/GO MCI may appear in both).
grounds: P-122 classifies pairs of scans from two time points while P-182 classifies a single baseline scan, so the input representation differs (the C-80 precedent).
P-122's accuracy is computed over longitudinal samples (823 from 275 subjects), not subjects, so the two accuracies do not measure the same quantity.
The progression criteria differ (3 years vs a follow-up of at least 18 months).

evidence_quotes.quote: In this task, the model achieved an accuracy of 75.85% and an AUC of 0.777 (Fig. 2B)
This dataset was labeled as either stable MCI (sMCI) or progressive MCI (pMCI) based on longitudinal diagnostic evaluations obtained at least 18 months apart.
The architecture synthesizes longitudinal sMRI data from dual temporal points
For the sMCI group, we gathered 449 longitudinal samples from 154 subjects diagnosed with sMCI. Similarly, the pMCI group con-sisted of 374 longitudinal samples from 121 subjects
and the remaining 15% (124 samples) for final model testing
Patients with pMCI are at a heightened risk of rapidly progressing to AD within the next three years

record_defects: The registry Modality 'MRI/PET' is wrong for both papers (sMRI only).

resolution_note says 'Confirmed genuine' on a 0.089 accuracy gap that ignores sample-level vs subject-level evaluation and the longitudinal input; the resolution field says 'Rejected - false positive' while the status is partially_resolved_candidate.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Subject-level accuracies from the same single-visit or same two-visit input and horizon in both studies, with non-overlapping uncertainty.
